story: At 5:17 on this humid, hazy Thursday in Sumter Oaks, Gary is heading home along Magnolia Loop with the patience of a man who has nowhere urgent to be. Donna, over at the Rec Center, is drilling third-shot drops on pickleball court one, determined to have her pointers ready when Gary arrives. Hal is out on the same street, dutifully counting the pink flamingos in Donna's flock and jotting down the total. Rosa, feeling relieved, is making her way to Town Square.
events: Donna (pickleball court 1): Practice third-shot drops so I can coach Gary when he arrives
Hal (donna flamingo flock): Count the flamingos visible from the street and note the total

gary.thought_process: I checked the bulletin board last tick and there was nothing from Architectural Review. Hal already knows the committee meets tomorrow, and Rosa has my sketches at the desk, so there's nothing more to ask him. Checking the board again within the hour would be silly. The cart stays in the garage until approval, so the useful thing is to head home and keep bench-testing the wiring, so I'm ready to install the minute they sign off. It also keeps me busy instead of fretting.

parameters.content: Heading back to the garage to keep bench-testing the cart wiring while I wait on the committee.

donna.thought_process: I've studied the ladder board, reserved a court for two hours (within the L-05 limit), and warmed up with dinking drills. Gary isn't in sight yet, so I shouldn't hunt for him or repeat my invitation from earlier. The best use of this hour is to keep practicing my third-shot drops so I'm ready to coach him when he shows up. Pruitt-Kowalski is the team to beat, and I want to be sharp.

parameters.content: Practice third-shot drops so I can coach Gary when he arrives

hal.thought_process: Gary's at the bulletin board and has already said he's keeping the cart in the garage until the committee signs off. Fair enough. The flamingos are right here on the street, and my goal is to document them for the committee. L-02 caps ornaments at three visible from the street. I've been counting for a while, and a proper count is exactly what I need on paper before I file. Go ahead and count them and get it done.

parameters.content: Count the flamingos visible from the street and note the total

rosa.thought_process: I've already handed the parade cart folder to the review desk last tick. The paperwork is in, and nobody else is here to talk to. Standing around won't speed up the review, and I still have a dinner to host and three neighbors to keep close. Better to head back toward the square and get on with the rest of my afternoon, instead of hovering at the desk.

parameters.content: Folder is filed, so I'm heading back to the square to find Donna and Gary and tell them it's in.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
